what_it_does: DRAM memory suffers from a phenomenon called row-hammer (repeated accesses to one row can corrupt nearby rows). Mitigation techniques depend on knowing each row's disturbance threshold — the number of accesses before corruption occurs. This paper measures real DRAM chips and discovers that thresholds are not fixed: they change unpredictably over time and temperature. Minimum thresholds can be 3.5 times lower than maximum, making static protection strategies ineffective. The paper characterizes this variability across 160 DDR4 and 4 HBM2 chips and evaluates dynamic mitigation approaches.
